teaser.text: Restaurant Brands International Inc. (RBI) is not one restaurant chain but a company built around four familiar quick-service brands and the businesses around them. To see how a dollar moves through RBI, start with what it sells, then follow who pays, where the economics are strongest, and what Tim Hortons adds.

stock.title: RBI stock forecast
stock.meta_description: RBI's weighted forecast is CAD 101.82 in October 2029, with bear, base and bull cases tied to franchisee health and execution.
stock.opening: RBI's probability-weighted price is CAD 101.82 in October 2029, including dividends. It hinges on whether RBI can restore franchisee economics.
stock.closing: The full RBI memo also covers RBI's business, its rivals, management's execution and the risks around the outcome.

blocks.heading: Where could RBI's shares be in October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted price is CAD 95.12 in October 2027, including dividends, versus today’s CAD 101.17. It rises to CAD 99.42 in October 2028 and CAD 101.82 in October 2029, producing a 12% three-year total return. The October 2029 range is wide: CAD 60.23 in the bear case to CAD 156.95 in the bull case. The probabilities are 30% bear, 55% base and 15% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for RBI?

paragraphs.text: Base earnings increase from $1,980 million in October 2027 to $2,110 million in October 2028 and $2,234 million in October 2029. The underlying revenue path rises from $9,900 million to $10,250 million, while normalized margins widen from 20.0% to 21.8%. The first-year estimate is close to the $9.89 billion consensus revenue forecast and below the roughly $2.04 billion implied by analyst EPS expectations. The bear case declines from $1,753 million to $1,694 million as revenue stagnates and margins compress. The bull case reaches $2,426 million as Burger King gains persist, Popeyes stabilizes and refranchising removes direct operating costs. First-half adjusted net income rose 14.4%, but the latest tax benefit was partly unusual.

blocks.heading: How much cash does RBI really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations reached US$1,714 million in 2025. After US$265 million of capital spending, RBI reported free cash flow of US$1,449 million. Finance-lease principal reduces that amount because it is another cash claim.

Stock compensation requires a further adjustment. RBI adds the expense back because issuing shares uses no cash immediately, but shareholders absorb dilution unless the company later repurchases shares. Deducting US$151 million of stock pay leaves an economic free-cash-flow figure of US$1,262 million.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for RBI?

paragraphs.text: The P/E ratio can make the stock look cheaper when reported profit rises for unusual reasons. RBI received tax benefits from internal reorganizations, while acquisition accounting creates charges and gains that do not neatly describe current restaurant demand. The investor therefore needs recurring earnings, not merely the profit printed in one period.

dividend.title: RBI dividend: history and cash coverage
dividend.meta_description: RBI's dividend history, cash coverage, payout plans, and current yield in one clear view.
dividend.opening: RBI's dividend rose each year from $2.12 in 2021 to $2.48 in 2025, and the 2026 target is $2.60. RBI's dividend is covered by cash, but only narrowly: dividends and exchangeable partnership-unit distributions consumed US$1,108 million, leaving about US$305 million before other uses.
dividend.closing: The full RBI memo also answers how RBI's business works, how its rivals compare, how management is executing, and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: How much does RBI pay in dividends over time?

paragraphs.text: The dividend grows slowly in the base case, from $2.60 to $2.76 and then $2.92. That reflects 6% annual growth, below management’s operating-income ambition, while the company targets a durable dividend and roughly 60% payout ratio. The bear case holds at $2.60 before cutting to $2.34 if cash pressure persists. The bull case reaches $3.10 as investment needs fall. The recent dividend rose each year from $2.12 in 2021 to $2.48 in 2025, and the 2026 target is $2.60.

blocks.heading: Does RBI's dividend fit its free cash flow?

paragraphs.text: Across 2021–2025, dividends and buybacks absorbed almost all the free cash flow shown in the schedule. In 2023, distributions exceeded that year’s free cash flow, while net debt at the end of the period was slightly higher than at the beginning. Acquisitions also arrived in bursts, and debt issued in 2024 largely reflected refinancing rather than new spending power.

After capital spending and finance-lease principal, 2025 free cash flow was US$1,413 million. Dividends and exchangeable partnership-unit distributions consumed US$1,108 million, leaving about US$305 million before other uses.

blocks.heading: What is RBI's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Revenue has grown across the five-year span, but operating margin narrowed and the company’s own free cash flow as a share of revenue fell. Diluted EPS has retreated from its 2023 high. Net debt was US$12,416 million in 2025. The company’s own free cash flow yield is 4.4% before stock-based pay and 3.9% after it. The dividend yield is 3.7%, while the buyback yield is 0.0%.

earnings.title: RBI earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: RBI's next results are expected October 29, 2026; see guidance, recent results and what to watch.
earnings.opening: RBI's next results are expected on October 29, 2026. RBI's key watch is whether franchisee profitability improves while cash covers investment and distributions.
earnings.closing: The full RBI memo also answers how RBI's business works, who its rivals are, how its management is aligned, and what risks matter.

paragraphs.text: Management targets 8.0% organic Adjusted Operating Income growth and 4.0x net leverage in 2026, alongside US$1,600 million of total shareholder returns.

RBI guides to US$400 million of capex and cash inducements. The commitment covers 2026 and 2027. It expects annual investment of about US$300 million from 2028. The Q3 call, preliminarily scheduled for October 29, 2026, will test profit growth, franchisee economics and cash generation. RBI expects 300–500 U.S. company-operated Burger King restaurants by the end of 2027. Multibillion-dollar debt maturities begin in 2028.

blocks.heading: Has RBI kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: RBI reaffirmed a target of at least 8% organic adjusted operating-income growth across the 2024–2028 outlook period and reported growth above 8% in each of the first two years. That is progress, not a finished promise. RBI also changed the starting date used in special awards for Kobza and Siddiqui, so shareholders should inspect award terms because they shape the difficulty of the target.

blocks.heading: What do RBI's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Underlying profit grew more slowly. Organic AOI increased 6.7%, and adjusted EPS rose 12.9%. The reported tax rate was negative 12.3% because of reorganization-related deferred-tax benefits. The comparison therefore contains both better trading and easier accounting conditions.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in RBI's next results?

paragraphs.text: The Q3 call, preliminarily scheduled for October 29, 2026, should show whether operating-profit growth improves and whether cash covers investment and distributions. The useful evidence will be franchisee profitability, completed remodels and successful transfers to operators able to maintain the restaurants.
